title: Inside a command
summary: Three states, initialize / execute / end, and isFinished as the condition.

say.never: A **command** is one action the robot does, with a clear start and a clear finish: drive 2 meters, turn to 90 degrees, shoot. You don't call it yourself. You hand it to WPILib, and WPILib runs it for you, 50 times a second.
say.bit: A command is one action with a start and a finish. WPILib runs it for you, 50 times a second.

marks.label: a whole action, as one object

say.never: At any moment a command is in one of three states. **Waiting**: nobody has started it yet. **Running**: WPILib is calling it every loop. **Finished**: it is done and never runs again (unless you start it fresh). Everything else in this guide is about how it moves from one state to the next.
say.bit: A command is waiting, running, or finished. The rest of this guide is how it moves between them.

say.never: The moment a command goes from waiting to running, WPILib calls `initialize()` **one time**. Use it to remember things about the starting situation. `DriveDistanceCommand` saves where the robot is right now, so later it can work out how far it has driven.
say.bit: `initialize()` runs once, when the command starts. Use it to remember the starting situation.

say.never: While the command is running, WPILib calls `execute()` over and over, once every 20 thousandths of a second. This is the working part. `TurnToAngleCommand` checks how far off it is and sets the turning speed, every loop, so it keeps correcting.
say.bit: `execute()` runs every 20 ms while the command is running. It's the working part.

marks.label: how far off are we, right now?

say.never: After each `execute()`, WPILib asks `isFinished()`, a yes or no question: "are we done?" That yes/no is the command's **condition**. While it says `false`, the command keeps running. The first time it says `true`, the command stops. If you never make it say `true`, the command runs forever.
say.bit: After every `execute()`, WPILib asks `isFinished()`. `false` means keep going. `true` means stop.

say.never: When `isFinished()` says yes, WPILib calls `end(interrupted)` **one time**, then the command is finished. Use it to clean up, usually by stopping the motors. `interrupted` is `false` when the command finished by itself, and `true` when something else cut it off early (a button let go, a timeout, another command taking over).
say.bit: `end(interrupted)` runs once at the finish. Stop the motors here. `interrupted` is true if it was cut short.

say.never: Read it as a story. `initialize` once. Then a loop: `execute`, ask `isFinished`, and if the answer is no, `execute` again. When the answer is yes, `end(false)` once and the command is finished. If something cuts it off, `end(true)` runs instead and it is finished the same way. `end` always runs, whichever way it stops.
say.bit: initialize once, then execute and isFinished in a loop, then end once. end always runs.

board.code:
initialize()
execute()   isFinished()? no
execute()   isFinished()? no
execute()   isFinished()? YES
end(false)

say.never: Read the finished one first. Hold down **Ctrl** and tap **P**. A small search box pops up at the top. Type `TurnToAngleCommand`, then press **Enter**. It finds any file by its name, so you never have to dig through folders.
say.bit: Read the finished one first. Press **Ctrl+P**, type `TurnToAngleCommand` and press Enter. Quick Open finds any file by name, so you never have to dig through folders.

say.never: Look through the code for `isFinished`. That is the yes/no condition that decides when this turn is over. Then find `execute` above it, the part that does the turning. When you've found both, press **I did it**.
say.bit: Find `isFinished` (the condition) and `execute` (the turning). Press I did it when you've found both.
